title: Reverse mode of `broadcast_in_dim` raises for non-increasing `broadcast_dimensions`

found: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/pull/5282 (merged 2020) and https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/pull/34877 (merged 2026-02) fixed other cases of the same transpose rule. This case is present after both.

description: Reverse mode of `lax.broadcast_in_dim` raises a `ValueError` if `broadcast_dimensions` is not increasing,
because the transpose rule returns a cotangent of the wrong shape.
The primal and forward mode are correct.
If the result shape equals the operand shape, even the primal is wrong.
expected: its shape rule only rejects duplicates, and its docstring uses `broadcast_dimensions=(1, 0)` as an implicit transpose.
Reverse mode should undo the permutation and return a cotangent of the operand's shape.
reproducer: # The primal and forward mode are correct.
# Reverse mode raises, because the cotangent has the shape of the result.
# actual:  ValueError: Expected cotangent type float32[3,2] but got float32[2,3]
cause: `_broadcast_in_dim_transpose_rule` sums the cotangent over the axes that are not in `broadcast_dimensions`
and restores the axes of size 1 with `expand_dims`.
`reduce_sum` leaves the remaining axes in the order of the result,
but the operand has them in the order of `broadcast_dimensions`.
The two orders agree only if `broadcast_dimensions` is increasing, and the rule never permutes the axes back.
fix: Transpose the summed cotangent back to the axis order of the operand.
lean: `Jax.Lax.broadcastInDimTranspose_correct` proves the rule correct if `broadcast_dimensions` is strictly increasing,
it returns a cotangent of shape `(2, 3)` for an operand of shape `(3, 2)`.
The domain check of `scripts/shapes.py` finds it in Lean: the cotangent that the transpose rule returns
does not have the shape of the operand.
